newsitem.title: CHINA: China shares end mostly lower on cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: China shares end mostly lower on cautious mood.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended generally lower on Wednesday with investors taking a more cautious attitude after solid gains over the past few days, brokers said.
But Shanghai's B share index edged up 0.235 points, or 0.34 percent, to 68.726 points on volume of 23 million shares worth $9.7 million.

"Investors are cautious after the index failed to breach 69 points this afternoon," said one broker. "That level is regarded as a key resistance and if it is breached, B shares are likely to rise further.
"The market ignored the tumble in A shares late in the session which shows market sentiment is steady with investors buying shares for the long term," a second broker said.
"The market will move up further if there is no negative news in the short term, as the technical charts look very good," he said.
Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Device was the star performer of the day. Bargain-hunting saw its price jump $0.014, or 7.29 percent, to $0.206 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was the most traded counter on institutional buying. It gained $0.01, or 2.71 percent, to $0.378 on volume of 2.4 million shares.
Shanghai A shares fell sharply in the afternoon session on profit-taking after sharp gains over the past few weeks, brokers said. They added the market needed some time to correct in the short term.

The index slipped 17.325 points, or 1.55 percent, to 1,099.467 points on volume of 733.4 million shares worth seven billion yuan. The SSE30 index dipped 54.033 points, or 1.88 percent, to 2,820.326 points.
Tsingtao Brewery was the biggest loser on institutional selling. It slumped 0.39 yuan, or 5.27 percent, to 7.01 yuan on volume of 3.7 million shares.
Shenzhen's A share index closed sharply lower with investor confidence dented by an investigation into a major listed company suspected of accounting irregularities, brokers said.
The A share index slid 9.02 points, or 2.25 percent, to 391.26 on turnover of 7.91 billion yuan, compared to 10.81 billion yuan on Tuesday.
The B share index inched down 0.08 points, or 0.05 percent, to end at 154.92 points, with turnover falling to HK$55.25 million from Tuesday's HK$74.45 million.
Authorities are investigating Hainan Minyuan Agricultural Development Co for alleged violation of accounting rules in its 1996 annual report, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange suspended trading in the company's A shares pending the probe, the newspaper said.
"The report on Minyuan soured market sentiment," said one analyst. "Investors pulled funds out of the market to wait for the outcome of the investigation."
Brokers said B shares fell because institutions were reluctant to buy heavily in the corporate reporting season.
On Shenzhen's B share market, retailer Shenzhen International Enterprise was the worst performer, falling HK$0.15, or 2.73 percent, to HK$5.35 on volume of 120,300 shares.
Jiangling Motors bucked the trend, rising HK$0.11, or 2.95 percent, to HK$3.84 on volume of 385,300 shares. It was the day's biggest gainer.
On the A share market, chicken and feed processor Shenzhen Kondarl was the biggest loser, sliding 0.70 yuan, or 5.24 percent, to 12.65 with 2.61 million shares traded.
Brokers said new regulations aimed at tightening control over the market cooled speculation in many of the hot A stocks.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission on Tuesday announced a new rule banning anyone caught involved in insider trading and price rigging from the securities business.
